competences: The learner identifies key facts about the judiciary.
The learner explains information about Composition and roles of the judiciary using reference texts.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, spells, reads and writes judiciary, courts, magistrate, judge, law.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify facts about the judiciary.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to answer the available sourced questions about Composition and roles of the judiciary.
priorKnowledge: Learners have already studied Uganda and related Social Studies concepts. They build on this earlier work to learn about the judiciary.
materials: Primary Five SST reference on Composition and roles of the judiciary
references: P.5 Social Studies Lesson Notes Term III: Uganda as an Independent Nation

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the previous SST topic and introduces the judiciary. They ask "Give any two ways law brakers are punished by the Judiciary." and listen to learners' first responses before referring to the source notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall previously studied content and answer the opening question, explaining their ideas in short sentences.

steps.stage: Development: Meaning and key facts about the judiciary
steps.content: The judiciary arm of the government is the custodian of the law. The chief justice is assisted by the principal judge. Officials/ people who make up the judiciary Settles disputes and conflicts in courts of laws. It protects the rights of every citizen by giving free and fair trial in courts of law. To settle cases in courts of law Sentencing them to spend a period of time in prisons. Composition of the Judiciary. To punish law breakers. Composition of the judiciary Judiciary – court Punishes law breakers
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about the judiciary on the chalkboard, including "The judiciary arm of the government is the custodian of the law.; The chief justice is assisted by the principal judge. Officials/ people who make up the judiciary". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Features and related facts about the judiciary
steps.content: It makes sure that laws are observed and maintained in the country. . Interprets laws to the public. To ensure law and order in the country through the police and Judiciary. Right to fair hearing in courts of law. Lack of fair judgment in courts of law. This is a way of challenging election results in courts of law. Qualities of a voter in Uganda. Due to cancellation of results by courts of law. The principle judge To punish lawbreakers
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about the judiciary on the chalkboard, including "It makes sure that laws are observed and maintained in the country. .; Interprets laws to the public.". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Further facts about the judiciary
steps.content: To pass judgement Used to settle disputes in courts of law It is also hung up in the government places an instrument of power and authority.eg in the parliament, courts of law etc. To interpret laws to people. This is headed by the Chief magistrate. (iii) The High court. It is headed by the Principal judge (iv) The court of appeal. Apart from punishing law breakers, give any two other ways the Judiciary is important to a country. To interpret the law To decide if the law has been broken or not.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about the judiciary on the chalkboard, including "To pass judgement; Used to settle disputes in courts of law". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.content: Give any two ways law brakers are punished by the Judiciary. | Give one role of the judiciary arm of the government. How is a government important to | Who heads the Judiciary organ of government? | How does the Legislature help the Judiciary to perform its work? | What are bye laws?
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher gives the original questions, starting with "Give any two ways law brakers are punished by the Judiciary." and "Give one role of the judiciary arm of the government. How is a government important to". They monitor pupils as they answer, check responses against the source material and provide corrections.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the sourced exercise questions independently, consult their copied notes and correct any mistakes after marking.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the factual content on the judiciary, asks "Give any two ways law brakers are punished by the Judiciary." and follows up with "Give one role of the judiciary arm of the government. How is a government important to". They confirm the answers and assign the remaining sourced practice.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners state one important fact from their lesson notes, answer the final oral questions and correct their written work.

assessment: Use the original questions "Give any two ways law brakers are punished by the Judiciary." and "Give one role of the judiciary arm of the government. How is a government important to", along with other listed items, to assess learners' understanding and correct errors from the source material.
homework: Answer the remaining sourced question, including "Why should a country have laws?"
